To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the topography of Mars can have an impact on the apparent velocity structure and on the travel-time of surface waves; 2) effects are of the same order of magnitude as those of the Earth; 3) effects are larger for the Earth than for Mars due to the difference in mean crustal thickness.

the topographic relief of Mars can induce an apparent anomaly on the surface wave velocity of up to 1% and that this apparent anomaly is larger than the topographic effects on the Earth when using a crustal thickness of 50 km. the presence of topography can induce an apparent seismic velocity anomaly of 0.5%, that travel times of surface waves are increased for seismographs in the north hemisphere and decreased in the South hemisphere and that effects on Mars seismogram by the topography are larger than what is seen on the Earth due to the thinner crust of Mars.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the numerical study of the effects induced on surface waves by topography.
the numerical assessment of the effects on seismogram of the topography and crust–mantel discontinuities.
the effects of topographies of the surface and of the crust– mantle discontinuity on surface waves.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the crustal thickness has a stronger impact on seismograms than the topography of surface and crust– mantle discontinuities.
the topographic effects are significant, but not overwhelming and should be taken into account for future Mars seismic network design.
the effects induced by the topography are of the same order as the ones induced by the crustal structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
topography and crust–mantletopography are important to be taken into account in order to correctly interpret Mars seismograms.
the effects of topographic reliefs are not negligible and that they have to be taken into account in the interpretation of future seismological data.
the topography of Mars is not a major obstacle for the study of its interior structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the topography of Mars has to be taken into account to interpret seismograms recorded in a future Mars seismological network.

topographic effects are of importance when studying the interior structure of Mars and that the spectral element method coupled with a modal solution is a very efficient tool to study the effects of the topography on the seismograms.
topography effects on surface waves are not negligible and must be considered when analyzing future Mars seismic data.
